assignment: Prepare a facilities decision on a proposed load shift for a residential building.
source: A laundry bank draws 24 kW for two hours. Peak electricity costs $0.30/kWh and off-peak $0.12/kWh. Running after 22:00 conflicts with the quiet-hours policy. A daytime off-peak window exists on Saturday. Daily use varies, and moving demand does not change the energy per load. A peak-demand fee is based on the highest monthly half hour.

criteria.full: Calculates 48 kWh and up to $8.64 energy-charge savings per shifted cycle.
criteria.partial: Estimates savings direction but omits energy or uses the wrong tariff difference.

criteria.full: Separates time-of-use savings from total energy and conditional monthly maximum-demand savings.
criteria.partial: Says demand or emissions will fall automatically.

criteria.full: Considers the Saturday window and user access or capacity while respecting quiet hours.
criteria.partial: Suggests a cheap time without checking policy or residents' access.

criteria.full: Defines meter and usage observations and a review rule for a reversible pilot.
criteria.partial: Suggests monitoring without comparing shifted cycles or peaks.
